response.sql: SELECT c.state AS state, COUNT(*) AS matched_records, COUNT(*) * 1.0 / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER () AS share FROM player_college pc JOIN college c ON pc.college_id = c.college_id GROUP BY c.state

assumptions.assumption: Blank and NULL states are treated as separate groups, since the request only says a blank or missing state is its own group. NULL states form one group and empty-string states form another. Rows are not merged, and no trimming is applied.
Each player_college row counts as one record, so duplicate player/college rows are not deduplicated. If college_id is duplicated in college, those rows would inflate the matched counts.

alternatives.interpretation: Treat NULL and blank (empty or whitespace-only) states as a single group, shown as an empty string.
alternatives.sql: SELECT COALESCE(TRIM(c.state), '') AS state, COUNT(*) AS matched_records, COUNT(*) * 1.0 / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER () AS share FROM player_college pc JOIN college c ON pc.college_id = c.college_id GROUP BY COALESCE(TRIM(c.state), '')
